prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Britain faces immense challenges—debt, social breakdown and broken politics—but can be renewed if we pull together. This manifesto invites the country to “join the government of Britain,” shifting from big government to a Big Society where power is devolved to people, families, professionals and communities. Core beliefs: responsibility (fiscal, personal, social), enterprise and aspiration, and the conviction that society is not the state. The aim is transparent, accountable government that trusts people and delivers value.

Economy: Restore stability with a credible plan to cut the bulk of the structural deficit over a Parliament, safeguard Britain’s credit rating and keep interest rates low. Establish an independent Office for Budget Responsibility; hold an emergency budget; cut waste (not frontline services), restrain public pay and pensions at the top, and stop Labour’s “jobs tax” (NI rise) by cutting waste. Build a more balanced, green, hi‑tech, export‑led economy: simplify and lower business taxes, reduce red tape, open procurement to SMEs, boost apprenticeships, support innovation and science, encourage saving and fair pensions, and reform banking (bank levy, prudential supervision by the Bank of England, more SME credit). Invest in modern infrastructure: high‑speed rail, better commuter rail, superfast broadband without a phone tax, Heathrow linked not expanded.

Work and welfare: Replace failing schemes with a single Work Programme, reassess incapacity claims, pay providers by results, and require claimants to take reasonable jobs or community work—help up, not hand‑outs. Make work pay, back small firms (NI holiday for new hires), and support entrepreneurship.

Families and early years: Make Britain the most family‑friendly country. End the couple penalty in tax credits, recognize marriage and civil partnerships in the tax system, freeze council tax for two years, extend flexible working and shared parental leave, protect childhood from commercialisation, refocus Sure Start on early intervention, and fund 4,200 more health visitors.

NHS: Increase funding in real terms each year; put patients and clinicians in charge. Expand patient choice, GP‑led commissioning, payment by results, and publish outcome data. Scrap politically driven targets. Improve access (24/7 urgent care; extended GP hours), fight infections (more single rooms), create a Cancer Drugs Fund, integrate health and social care budgets for long‑term conditions, support carers, and prioritise public health.

Schools: Restore discipline and excellence. Raise teacher quality (Teach First, Troops to Teachers), protect heads’ authority, teach phonics with an early reading check, make curriculum and exams more rigorous, expand academies and allow new providers, introduce a pupil premium, strengthen technical education, protect special schools, and publish clear performance data.

Crime, borders and integration: Put victims and citizens first. Toughen knife crime sentences, cut police paperwork, elect local police commissioners, curb binge drinking, reform rehabilitation with payment by results, and create a Border Police Force. Reduce net migration to tens of thousands with an annual non‑EU limit, tighten student visas, and promote English and integration.

Political reform and localism: Clean up Westminster (recall MPs, curb lobbying, cut MPs and ministers’ pay), publish spending and salaries, slash quangos, and give citizens real power (petitions, public bill reading, local referendums, elected mayors). “Open‑source” planning, community rights to buy/run services, protect civil liberties (scrap ID cards, limit DNA retention, UK Bill of Rights).

Environment: “Vote blue, go green.” Create a Green Investment Bank and a household Green Deal; build a smart grid; back renewables, new nuclear (no subsidy) and CCS; protect habitats, reform CAP/CFP, uphold animal welfare, and drive toward a zero‑waste society.

National interest: Establish a National Security Council, support success in Afghanistan, renew Trident, fix defence procurement, and restore the Military Covenant. Pursue a liberal Conservative foreign policy—active abroad, strong with allies, human rights‑focused—be positive in the EU but transfer no more powers, lock any future transfers behind a referendum, bring powers back, never join the euro. Honour 0.7% aid with transparency, results, malaria focus and trade‑led development.
